intro: Pick components by what the product has to do, not by what looks nice. Each playbook lists the usual needs of a domain, the opendraft components and blocks that serve each one, and how well they fit: ready (use as is), adapt (works with the caveat given) or gap (nothing fits yet; build it from primitives and follow the domain principles).

domains.title: Security and compliance
domains.summary: Security operations, threat detection, access control and audit products. Used by analysts under pressure: dense data, fast triage, irreversible actions.
principles: Never show severity by color alone. Pair every severity color with a text label (Critical, High, Medium, Low) and use the same scale everywhere.

Show times as absolute UTC in `font-mono` with a relative hint (for example `14:02:09Z · 3 min ago`). Analysts compare timestamps across systems. `timeline` renders `time` in mono and takes an ISO `timestamp`.

Make destructive or far-reaching actions (isolate a host, revoke a session, delete a key) require a confirmation that names the consequence, and show who did it and when afterward. Do not offer 'Always allow' (`tool-approval`'s optional `onAlwaysAllow`) for these.
Mask secrets by default (tokens, keys, hashes). Use `secret-input` for entering or showing a secret (masked, with reveal, copy and optional auto-hide) and never log or echo the value.
Favor dense tables and a `command-palette` (Cmd/Ctrl+K) for jumping to an entity. Default these products to the dark theme (add the `dark` class), but keep both themes working.
Every state change should leave an audit trail the user can see. Plan for an audit-log screen from the start. Record who and when in your backend; the UI components only display it.
Show what the system knows, not what it concludes: label automated or AI verdicts as such and link the evidence. Do not state or imply that the product makes anyone compliant with a standard.

needs.notes: Start with the `data-table` block: `columns`, `rows`, `getRowId`, `searchable`, `filters` (a `filter-bar` config with chips and clear-all), `views` (tabs such as Open, Acknowledged, Closed), `selectable` with `bulkActions` (Acknowledge, Close, Assign receive the selected rows) and a card layout when narrow. Render severity and status as `badge` (with `dot`) in a column `cell`. For a very large live stream use the virtualized `table` (pass `rowHeight` and `height` or `maxHeight`) with `filter-bar` above and `bulk-action-bar` shown when ids are selected.
needs.gap: `data-table` pages its rows rather than virtualizing them, so it suits thousands of rows, not an unbounded stream. There is no four-level severity component (use `badge`: Critical to `destructive`, High and Medium to `warning`, Low to `secondary`, always with the word) and no saved-filter control: store the `filter-bar` value yourself.

needs.need: Investigate an incident: timeline of events and evidence
needs.notes: `timeline` is the event feed: per item `time` (mono), ISO `timestamp`, `title`, `description`, `meta` (actor or source), `status` (default, success, warning, destructive, current, upcoming; markers are never color only) and expandable `children` for raw evidence. Use `align="right-time"` for a time column, `collapsible` with `max` for long lists, and pass events newest first yourself (`newestFirst` only changes the label). `code-block` shows a raw event or command, `file-diff` a config change, `stepper` (horizontal or vertical) the response stages.

`approval-card` takes a `title`, body `children` and `onApprove`, `onRequestChanges`, `onReject` (the last two render only when passed), a controlled `status` and a `result` slot where you put 'Approved by X at 14:02:09Z'. Use `tool-approval` when an AI agent proposes an action: it lists `parameters` and has allow once and deny. For the dangerous ones, build a `dialog` with an `input` the user types the host name into, and keep the confirm `Button` disabled until it matches (the type-to-confirm in `settings-page`'s danger zone does this). `sonner` reports the result.
needs.gap: No built-in typed-confirmation or two-person approval component: assemble it from `dialog` + `input` + `button`. Who approved and when comes from your backend.

needs.notes: `settings-page` with `sections={["team"]}` gives a member list, invite (`onInvite`) and role change. Use `permission-matrix` for the custom-roles screen: `roles` by `groups` of permissions, select-all per role, row and group, read-only built-in roles and a change summary to review before saving (`onValueChange`). Long user lists belong in `data-table`. `repeater-field` edits rule lists such as allowed IP ranges.
needs.gap: `settings-page` roles are fixed to owner, admin, member and viewer; use `permission-matrix` for anything custom. The matrix edits grants only: who may change roles, and enforcement, come from your backend.

needs.need: Search and review an audit log
needs.notes: `data-table` with `searchable`, `filters` (actor, action, outcome as select or multi-select), sortable mono columns for IDs and times, and `onRowOpen` to show one entry in a `description-list` (actor, target, IP, request ID with `copyable`). Show a change with `file-diff` and one entity's history with `timeline`. Use `date-range-picker` for the day range and `date-time-picker` (with a named `timeZone`, UTC by default here) for exact from and to bounds.
needs.gap: No dedicated audit-log viewer with live tail, saved queries or export; assemble it from `data-table` and `filter-bar`, and page from your backend. `date-range-picker` itself has no time of day, which is why the exact bounds use `date-time-picker`.

needs.need: Show security posture and compliance coverage
needs.notes: `stat` and `StatGroup` for headline numbers, with `delta` and `goodWhen="down"` for counts where fewer is better. `gauge` shows a posture or risk score with `thresholds` bands and a text status (never color alone). `progress` for control coverage: set `invert` with `tone="auto"` where a low value is bad. `time-series-chart` plots findings over time with `thresholds`, brush zoom and a data-table fallback. `analytics-dashboard` can still frame a findings overview through `labels`, `metrics`, `rows` and `channels`; pass `fill={false}` inside a scrolling page.
needs.gap: `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7d, 30d and 90d and its table columns are fixed to name, visitors, conversion and duration (relabel or replace the last with `valueColumn`). Prefer `time-series-chart` when you need your own series. Do not present a score as proof of compliance with a standard.

needs.need: Sign in with SSO and MFA
needs.notes: `auth-screen` handles email and password, remember me, forgot password and provider buttons (`providers`, `onProvider`); `onSubmit` may throw to show an error. After it succeeds, show `mfa-step` for the second factor: `methods` (authenticator app, SMS, security key), `onVerify` (async, returns the result), `onResend` with a countdown, and verifying, error and `locked` states. Use an `alert` for session-expired or lockout notices.
needs.gap: `mfa-step` collects and submits a code but the verification, rate limits and lockout come from your auth provider or backend. There is no passkey enrolment screen or SSO-by-domain flow.

needs.notes: List keys in `data-table` with created, last used and a `badge` for status (never show the full secret in a row). Reveal a new key once in a `dialog` with `secret-input` (masked, reveal, `copyable`, `autoHideMs`), a `copy-button` and an `alert` that it will not be shown again. Revoke with a type-to-confirm `dialog`.

needs.need: Show active incidents and degraded feeds
needs.notes: `alert` has variants default, info, success, warning and destructive, a `banner` mode for full-width notices, an `AlertAction` slot for a button and optional `dismissible`.

needs.need: Ask an AI analyst to summarize or investigate
needs.notes: `agent-workspace` takes your `conversations`, `messages`, `tasks` and an async `onSend` that returns the reply (thinking rows, tool steps, streamed `answer` tokens, `sources`, `followUps`). Show evidence with `citations` and gate any action behind `approval-card` or `tool-approval`.

needs.need: Show assets or attack paths on a map
needs.notes: `map-view` is a token-styled MapLibre GL map: pass `markers` (each with a text `label` and a `status`), `routes` and `areas`, and use `selectedId` with `onSelect` to sync it with a `data-table` of assets. It includes a keyboard-reachable list of the same locations, so the map is never the only view.
needs.gap: `map-view` is geographic only. There is no network or attack-path graph (`flowchart` is a workflow canvas). Use a graph library (see integrations) for nodes and edges and keep the entity list in `data-table` beside it.

integrations.note: Draw nodes and edges with our tokens for color and type; keep the severity text labels.
map-view is already built on MapLibre GL JS; reach for deck.gl only for very dense layers. Always give each marker a text label for assistive technology.
Use time-series-chart for multi-series trends with thresholds and zoom. uPlot copes with very large series; the chart inside analytics-dashboard is fixed to its own metrics.
Put the provider's flow behind the auth-screen block (onSubmit and onProvider) and use mfa-step for the second factor, wiring onVerify to the provider.

domains.title: IT, DevOps and infrastructure
domains.summary: Monitoring, incident management, deployments, logs and internal tools for engineers and IT teams.
principles: Status needs a word and a shape, not just a color: Operational, Degraded, Down, Maintenance. `status-indicator` already uses exactly this vocabulary (plus Unknown) with a distinct shape per state; keep one vocabulary across the product.

Show times in UTC with `font-mono`, and let the user switch to local time in one place (a single setting or toggle that every screen reads; `settings-page` has a timezone select in its profile section).
Numbers that change should use `tabular-nums` so columns don't jitter; use `animated-number` sparingly on dashboards, never in tables or logs.

Long-running work (deploys, migrations) shows progress, current step and a way to cancel. Never leave a spinner with no step. Cancel is a `Button` you add; none of the progress components includes one.
Provide a copy button next to every ID, command, hash and URL.
Treat logs and code as data: monospaced, wrap toggle, selectable, searchable. `code-block` has a `wrap` prop and line numbers; search and filtering are yours to build.
Never put real secrets in props that end up in client bundles or logs; show masked values and fetch reveals on demand.

needs.notes: `StatusIndicator` (`status` operational, degraded, down, maintenance, unknown; optional `pulse`) next to each service name, and `UptimeBar` for the 90-day bars: pass `segments` (one `{status, label}` per day), `uptime` text and `name` for the accessible summary. `stat` tiles for headline numbers, `gauge` (with `thresholds` and a text status) or `progress` for utilization and quota, `alert` (info or warning, `banner`) for planned maintenance.
`alert` banner for the current incident, `StatusIndicator` and `UptimeBar` per component, and `timeline` for past incident updates (newest first, `collapsible` with `max`).

Incident list in `data-table` (severity and status as `badge` cells, `views` for Open, Mitigated, Resolved, `filters` for service and severity). Incident updates in `timeline` (`status` warning, destructive, current, success; expandable `children` for notes). Lifecycle stages (Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved) in `stepper`. Runbook steps in `checklist` (tickable items, per-item notes, progress and a sign-off step). The on-call rota is a `scheduler` block: `resources` are people or teams, `events` are shifts, with conflict marking and keyboard moves.
needs.gap: No paging or acknowledge control and no escalation policy editor; those come from your paging service. `scheduler` draws the rota but overrides and swaps are your logic.

needs.notes: Use the virtualized `table` with fixed `rowHeight`, mono cells, a level `badge` column, `onEndReached` and `loading` for paging, and `filter-bar` above it for level, service and text filters (chips with clear-all). `code-block` (`showLineNumbers`, `highlightLines`, `wrap`, `maxHeight`, `copyable`, `status="streaming"`) shows one entry's full payload or a stack trace. `code-panel` is not suited: it is a small sample-shaped card capped at about 420px wide.
needs.gap: No log viewer. There is no follow or live-tail mode, so you append rows to `data` and manage scroll position yourself; no match highlighting; columns hide into a sideways scroll on phones (use `data-table`'s card layout only for modest result sets).

needs.notes: `time-series-chart` is the metric chart: several `series` of `{t, v}` points (null `v` leaves a gap), a named `timeZone` (UTC by default here), `thresholds` for an SLO or alert line, brush zoom (`onZoomChange`), keyboard stepping and a data-table fallback. `analytics-dashboard` still gives KPI cards with deltas and a ranked table; relabel it through `labels` and feed it `data` per range. `date-range-picker` takes YYYY-MM-DD dates.
needs.gap: No auto-refresh or live streaming in the chart: replace `series` as new points arrive. `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7d, 30d and 90d and its table columns are name, visitors, conversion and duration (swap the last for `valueColumn`). For millions of points use a canvas chart library (see integrations).

needs.notes: Stages in a `stepper` (use `description` for the commit, duration or environment). Pre-deploy and post-deploy checks in `checklist` (tickable, with a sign-off step). Deploy history in `timeline`. Gate production with `approval-card`; show the change with `file-diff`. Add your own Cancel `Button`.
needs.gap: No pipeline or dependency graph. `flowchart` is NOT a status graph: it is an editable Trigger and If/Else workflow canvas with draggable cards and condition chips. `task-rows` is payment-shaped (label, amount, details) and does not fit.

needs.notes: `repeater-field` (`value`, `renderRow`, `createItem`, `min`, `max`) for key and value rows, with an `input` for the name and a `secret-input` for the value (masked, reveal, optional auto-hide). Show a config change before saving with `file-diff`. Use `dialog` to confirm changes to production.
needs.gap: No dedicated environment editor: no .env import, per-environment inheritance or secret rotation. Fetch reveals on demand from your backend.

needs.need: Inventory of servers, services or assets
needs.notes: Virtualized `table` for thousands of rows: sortable, resizable and reorderable columns, `selectable` with `onSelectionChange`, inline `editable` cells with `onCellEdit`. Put `filter-bar` above it and show `bulk-action-bar` (count, actions, clear) when rows are selected. For a few hundred rows the `data-table` block does all of this with paging and a card layout on phones.

`command-palette` runs actions (items with `onSelect`, groups, hints and keywords). `code-block` can show command output, appended as it streams (`status="streaming"`). `agent-screen` is NOT a terminal: it is a card that views an agent's remote screen image or video.
needs.gap: No terminal emulator (no PTY, ANSI colors or input line). Embed one such as xterm.js if users need a real shell.

needs.notes: Pass the real workspace name, members and billing; `sections` chooses which tabs show. Team roles are fixed to owner, admin, member and viewer.
Supply `conversations`, `messages` and an `onSend` that returns the reply. Ask for approval (`approval-card` or `tool-approval`) before any action that changes production.

integrations.note: time-series-chart covers multi-series metrics with thresholds, zoom and a table fallback. For heavier dashboards wrap the library so colors come from CSS variables, and keep a table fallback for accessibility.
The Table is already virtualized; for millions of lines the filtering and paging belong server-side (feed it with onEndReached).
Use stepper or timeline for linear pipelines and a graph library when stages branch or users must pan and zoom.
opendraft has no terminal; theme xterm.js with the code font and background tokens.
Update rows in place and highlight what changed without moving the layout under the cursor.

domains.title: Aviation and travel operations
domains.summary: Airline and airport operations, flight information, booking and check-in, crew and maintenance tools. Safety-critical context: clarity and correctness beat flourish.
principles: State times with an explicit zone. Use 24-hour time, mark UTC as `Z`, and show the airport's local time beside it. Never leave a time ambiguous. `date-time-picker` picks a date and time in a named IANA `timeZone` (with DST gap and overlap handling and an other-zone readout); `eta-indicator`, `time-series-chart` and `scheduler` also take a `timeZone`. Store the zone with every time you save.
Flight status is always a word first (On time, Delayed, Boarding, Departed, Cancelled) with a color second (`badge` with `dot`). Show the reason and the new time for any delay.
Use IATA or ICAO codes in `font-mono` with the full name on hover or beneath, for example `LIS` and Lisbon.

On safety-critical screens (maintenance sign-off, checklists, weather) avoid decorative motion (skip `text-scramble` and `animated-number`), show who signed and when, and require an explicit confirm. Prefer `approval-card` over a quiet toggle. These screens record a sign-off; they do not replace your approved maintenance or operational records system.
Design for tablets, gloves and bright light: large touch targets, high contrast, no hover-only information.
A live board updates in place without shifting the layout under a user's cursor. Highlight what changed, then settle. No component does the highlight for you.

needs.notes: `data-table` with a sortable time column, mono code and flight-number cells (`mono`), a status `badge` (`dot`) in a column `cell`, `views` for Departures and Arrivals, `filters` for airline, terminal and status, and a card layout on narrow screens. `text-scramble` can resolve a changed gate or time to its new text. `alert` for a disruption banner. For a very long board use the virtualized `table` with `filter-bar` instead.
needs.gap: No split-flap display. No built-in highlight when a row changes: flash the changed cell yourself, then settle.

needs.notes: `record-page` is the flight detail: `title` (flight number), `status` (a word first), `summary` stats for scheduled and estimated times, gate and aircraft, `fields`, `activity` as the leg-by-leg `timeline` and `related` for connecting flights. `eta-indicator` shows the estimated arrival as a range with a confidence word and a stale state, in a named `timeZone`. `map-view` can draw the route as a `routes` line between airports. Put `alert` above for the delay reason and new time. `detail-page` is NOT this: it is an event-ticket purchase page.
needs.gap: `map-view` draws straight routes between coordinates on a street-style basemap; it does not animate a live aircraft position or great-circle arcs, and you supply flight data from your provider.

needs.notes: Form built from `field` / `FieldGroup`: origin and destination, one date with `date-picker` or an outbound and return range with `date-range-picker` (YYYY-MM-DD, no time of day), passengers with `quantity-stepper`, cabin with `radio-group` or `select`. Use `date-time-picker` where a departure time in a named zone matters. For an airport picker, a controlled `command-palette` (`open`, `onOpenChange`, items with IATA codes in `keywords`, `onSelect` sets the field) is a workable hack. Render results in `data-table` with a select `Button` in a `cell`.
needs.gap: No airport or route picker and no fare comparison grid. `catalog` is NOT a flight list: its items are events {title, host, location, category, date, price, capacity, remaining}, with no origin, destination or times.

needs.notes: `checkout` is event-booking shaped: fixed fields (name, email, phone, an optional attendee, delivery by email or desk, pay by card or later) and a cart of items with quantity, fees and discount codes. It cannot collect per-passenger details such as date of birth or travel documents. Build a `stepper` wizard with one `FieldSet` per passenger (`repeater-field` for several, or a loop), `date-picker` for dates of birth, `select` for title and nationality, `checkbox` for consents, and `address-form` for a billing or contact address. Take payment with your provider's hosted fields.
needs.gap: No passenger form and no payment step that fits a flight booking; do not push passenger data through `checkout`.

needs.notes: `order-confirmation` can be relabelled as a booking confirmation through `labels` (title, order number, buttons) and `order` (lines with price, `tickets` with `fields` and a `code`). It shows one `ticket-pass` per ticket.
needs.gap: It is ticket-shaped with a fixed 3-step stepper (`labels.steps` renames the three steps, you cannot add or remove one), a stat row for date, tickets and total, and a QR code per ticket.

needs.notes: `ticket-pass` takes `title`, `eyebrow`, free-form `fields` (Gate, Seat, Group, Boards at, Terminal), `code`, `status` (valid, used, expired, void), `dark`, `tone` and an `actions` slot. The QR drawn is real and encodes `code`.
needs.gap: It draws only a QR code. Airline boarding passes use a PDF417, Aztec or QR code carrying data formatted and issued by the airline's system; encode only what your airline system gives you, and use a barcode library for other symbologies. Treat this as a display of the pass, not the credential.

needs.notes: `seat-map` is a keyboard-navigable grid picker: `layout` (rows and aisles, `rowLabels`, `columnLabels`), per-seat `seats` with state (available, occupied, blocked, premium), optional `price` and `tier`, `value` / `onChange` for the selection, `max` for the passenger count, a legend and a running total. Every state has a text label as well as a shape. Load the cabin layout and availability from your reservation system and re-check at payment.

`scheduler` block for the roster: `resources` are crew members, `events` are duties and rest periods (`status` word plus `tone`), day and week views, conflict marking, drag or keyboard moves (`onEventMove`) and an agenda on narrow widths. Give it the airport zone through `timeZone`. `gantt` suits a multi-day pairing or rotation plan with groups. `data-table` lists the crew with a duty `badge` per day.
needs.gap: `scheduler` marks overlaps only; duty-time limits, rest rules and qualification checks must come from your crew-planning system, never from the UI.

needs.notes: `checklist` for pre-flight and maintenance items: tickable rows with `notes`, progress, `onComplete` and a sign-off step that stays disabled until every item is done. Capture photos with `photo-capture` (camera or file, optional captions) and documents with `dropzone`. `signature-pad` takes a drawn or typed signature; `approval-card` records the sign-off (its `result` slot can show 'Signed by X at 08:14Z'). History in `timeline` and `data-table`. `todo-list` is NOT a checklist: it is a read-only display of an agent's task plan.
needs.gap: Who signed and when must come from your authenticated backend and be written by it; a captured signature image is not a credential. These screens record a sign-off, they do not replace your approved maintenance records system.

needs.notes: `alert` has info, warning and destructive variants, a `banner` mode and an `AlertAction` slot (for example a View affected flights button). Pass bulletin text as supplied by your data source, with its issue and validity times in UTC, and link to the source.

On-time performance and disruption counts in `StatGroup` tiles (`delta` with `goodWhen`). `StatusIndicator` for airport or system status, `gauge` for stand or gate utilisation, `time-series-chart` for movements per hour in the airport zone with a capacity `threshold`, `map-view` for an airport or network status map (status markers with text labels), and `data-table` for the exceptions list.
needs.gap: `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7d, 30d and 90d and its table columns are name, visitors, conversion and duration; prefer `time-series-chart` here. `map-view` is not a radar or live-traffic display.

integrations.note: map-view draws routes as straight lines between coordinates; great-circle arcs, tracks and live traffic are a map-library job (deck.gl). Keep times and codes in the table beside it.
Normalize to UTC and show local airport time beside it.
date-time-picker picks and displays a time in a named IANA zone (DST gaps and overlaps handled). Use one of these to convert and format stored instants elsewhere.
qr-code only draws QR. bwip-js can render PDF417 and Aztec; scanning is a separate job, for example with zxing-js.

scheduler (resource day and week views) and gantt (task bars with dependencies) cover rosters and maintenance plans. Embed one of these only for what they lack, such as recurrence rules or very large resource timelines.

domains.title: Logistics, supply chain and fleet
domains.summary: Shipment tracking, dispatch, warehouse and fleet products for operators, drivers and customers who need to know where things are and when they'll arrive.
principles: Every shipment shows three things at a glance: status (as a word), where it is, and when it will arrive (an ETA with a confidence or a delay reason). `eta-indicator` shows the estimate as a range with a confidence word and a stale state; `map-view` shows where.
Tracking IDs, container numbers and SKUs go in `font-mono` with a `copy-button`.
Exceptions come first: delayed, held and failed deliveries sort to the top (sort your data; `tabs` for Exceptions first) and carry the reason and the next action.

Show dates and times in the location's own time zone, and say which zone. `date-time-picker` picks a time in a named IANA `timeZone` and can show the same moment in other zones; `eta-indicator` and `scheduler` take a `timeZone` too. Store the zone with the instant.

Operators work in bulk: lists need row selection with a bulk action bar and filters that survive a reload. `data-table` has `selectable` with `bulkActions`, and `bulk-action-bar` and `filter-bar` stand alone for other layouts; persist the filter value yourself.

Driver and warehouse screens are used one-handed on a phone: large targets, one primary action per screen, works on a poor connection. `data-table` switches to a card layout when narrow; the virtualized `table` still scrolls sideways, so avoid it on driver screens.

needs.notes: `detail-page` is NOT this: it is an event-ticket purchase page. Compose: `site-header`, a `card` with the tracking ID plus `copy-button` and a status `badge`; `eta-indicator` for the estimate (range, confidence word, stale and past-window states, destination `timeZone`); `map-view` for the last known position and route (with a text list of the same stops); `stepper` for milestones with `description` carrying 'time zone · place'; `description-list` for carrier, service and weight; `alert` for a delay or exception. A `timeline` (`time`, ISO `timestamp`, `meta` for the location, `status`) is the better fit for the full scan history. For an internal view of one shipment use the `record-page` block.
needs.gap: No ready-made tracking page; compose it from the pieces. Position and ETA values come from your carrier or telematics data; `map-view` does not animate live movement.

needs.need: Manage a list of shipments or orders
needs.notes: `data-table` block: `columns` (status `badge` and a mono ID with `copy-button` in column `cell`s), `searchable`, `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for carrier, lane, date), `views` for Exceptions, In transit, Delivered, `selectable` with `bulkActions` (Reassign, Hold, Export receive the selected rows), paging and a card layout on phones. Sort exceptions first in your data. For tens of thousands of rows use the virtualized `table` with `filter-bar` and `bulk-action-bar`.
needs.gap: No saved filters: keep the `filter-bar` value in your own state or URL.

needs.notes: Two views of the same jobs. `scheduler` block: `resources` are drivers or vehicles, `events` are jobs on a day or week axis, with conflict marking, drag or keyboard reassignment (`onEventMove`) and an agenda on narrow widths. `stage-board` block: columns for Unassigned, Assigned, In transit, Delivered with drag or keyboard moves, WIP `limit`s, per-stage totals and a detail panel. Show unassigned jobs in a `data-table` beside the scheduler.
needs.gap: Neither does route optimisation or capacity checks; the UI marks time overlaps only, and assignment rules and ETAs come from your dispatch system.

needs.notes: Wizard with `stepper`; `address-form` for pickup and delivery addresses (per-country rules, postal validation, autocomplete tokens); packages as rows in `repeater-field` (weight, size, quantity with `quantity-stepper`). Pickup window with `date-time-picker` in the pickup location's `timeZone`. Finish with `order-confirmation` relabelled as a booking confirmation (`labels`, `order.lines`, `order.tickets` with `fields` and a `code`).
needs.gap: `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped with a fixed 3-step stepper (rename only) and a QR per ticket. `checkout` is event-booking shaped (name, email, phone, attendee, card) and does not fit. `address-form` does not look up or autocomplete addresses from a provider.

needs.notes: `StatGroup` for utilization and on-time rate (`delta`, `goodWhen`). `map-view` for vehicle positions: `markers` with a text `label` and `status`, `selectedId` synced to a `data-table` of drivers and vehicles with `avatar` and `StatusIndicator` cells. `gauge` or `progress` for hours or fuel. `analytics-dashboard` works if the shape is KPIs, a trend per metric, a ranked list and a share breakdown; relabel via `labels`, `valueColumn` and the format props.
needs.gap: `map-view` shows the positions you pass; it has no live tracking, clustering of thousands of vehicles or geofencing. `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7d, 30d and 90d.

needs.notes: `table` with `editable` columns and `onCellEdit` for counts (`editable` is ignored on a column that sets `cell`), `filter-bar` for zone and SKU. Zones as `progress` or `gauge`: the default `tone="auto"` measures consumption, so a nearly full zone turns warning then destructive; for stock remaining set `invert`. A hardware scanner that types like a keyboard can fill an `input`.
needs.gap: No camera barcode scan input and no heat map of locations.

needs.notes: Recipient name in `field` and `input`; a signature with `signature-pad` (drawn or typed name; `onSign` returns the result); photos of the parcel with `photo-capture` (camera or file, `max`, optional captions; `onChange` gives the files); a failure reason in `select`. `qr-code` can show a handover code the recipient presents. Upload the files and stamp time, location and driver from your backend. `qr-code` only generates codes; scanning is a device job.

Compose: rate options in `data-table` (carrier, service, transit time, price in mono, a select `Button` in a `cell`) or `radio-group` cards, totals in `stat`, invoices in `data-table` with a status `badge`. `checkout` is NOT a quote flow: it is an event-booking checkout with fixed contact and payment fields.
needs.gap: No rate-comparison table and no quote or invoice component.

needs.need: ETA with confidence or delay reason
needs.notes: `eta-indicator` takes `eta`, optional `earliest` and `latest` (drawn as a range bar), a numeric `confidence` mapped to a high, medium or low word with an icon (never color alone), `updatedAt` with a stale state after `staleAfterMs`, a past-window state, and a `timeZone`. Add a `badge` for On time, At risk or Delayed and an `alert` with the reason for a delay. The estimate and confidence are computed by your backend.

Relabel `analytics-dashboard` (shipments, on-time rate, cost per delivery) through `labels`, `data` per range, the format props and `valueColumn` for cost. For your own series (volume per hour, on-time rate against a target) use `time-series-chart`: several series, `thresholds`, brush zoom, a named `timeZone` and a data-table fallback.
needs.gap: `analytics-dashboard` range tabs are fixed at 7d, 30d and 90d (so no `date-range-picker` link) and its table columns are page-analytics shaped (name, visitors, conversion, duration).

integrations.note: map-view is built on MapLibre GL JS and draws markers, routes and areas. For clustering, geofencing or traffic layers reach for the library directly; keep ETA and status in opendraft components.
Map each carrier's status codes to one status vocabulary before it reaches the UI.
Scanning is a device capability; opendraft's qr-code only generates codes and photo-capture takes pictures.
signature-pad and photo-capture cover proof of delivery; use a library only for exotic needs such as vector signature export.

integrations.for: Drag and drop for a dispatch board
integrations.note: stage-board has drag and keyboard moves built in; add dnd-kit only for cross-board or multi-select dragging.
date-time-picker handles a named zone; use one of these to convert and format stored instants elsewhere.

domains.title: Healthcare and patient care
domains.summary: Clinical and patient-facing health products: EHR views, scheduling, telehealth and patient portals. Clinicians work under time pressure with safety-critical data; patients need calm, plain-language screens.
principles: Show patient identity on every clinical screen: full name, date of birth and an identifier in `font-mono`, in a header that stays pinned (wrap it in your own `sticky top-0 bg-background` container; `page-header` is not sticky by itself). Wrong-patient errors are the failure to design against.

Always print units and reference ranges beside a measurement (`5.4 mmol/L, ref 3.9 to 5.6`), and never round or reformat a value without saying so. Do not rely on color alone to mark an abnormal or critical value; pair it with a text flag such as High, Low or Critical.

Critical values and allergy warnings stay visible until a named user acknowledges them. Never auto-dismiss a clinical alert or put one in a toast. Use a persistent `alert` (it only gets a close button if you pass `dismissible`, so don't) with an acknowledge `button` in `AlertAction`, and have your backend record who acknowledged it and when.
Privacy by default: mask identifiers and sensitive fields until revealed, keep reveals logged, and avoid showing patient names in browser titles, notifications and URLs.
Write patient-facing copy in plain language at a low reading level, explain medical terms in place, and say what happens next. Lead with the answer (`Your results are normal`), not the data.

Confirm irreversible or high-risk actions (sign an order, discharge, cancel a procedure) in a `dialog` that names the patient and the consequence. Where your rules require it, keep an audit trail of who viewed or changed a record.

opendraft is presentation only. It does not check doses, interactions or reference ranges and it makes no clinical-safety or privacy-law guarantee. Every value, flag and warning must come from your system of record, and you remain responsible for clinical validation.

State the time zone wherever a time is shown or chosen. `date-time-picker` picks a date and time in a named IANA zone (it handles DST gaps and overlaps), and `time-series-chart` and `scheduler` take a `timeZone`. Show when a result was last updated.

needs.notes: The `record-page` block gives the chart shell: header with `title`, `id` and `status`, `summary` stats for latest vitals (value with units, hint for the reference range or time taken), `fields` (a `description-list`: date of birth, sex, MRN with `copyable` and `mono`), an `activity` timeline and `related` items; extra `tabs` for Orders, Notes and Results. Add `avatar` and `badge` for name, age and flags, a persistent `alert` for allergies, and `gauge` for a single score with a text status.
needs.gap: No patient-banner component and nothing is sticky: wrap the banner in your own sticky container so it never scrolls away.

needs.need: Lab results and vitals with abnormal flags
needs.notes: `data-table` with columns for test, value with unit, range, flag and date, a text-labelled `badge` (High, Low, Critical) in the `cell`, `filters` by panel or flag and a card layout on phones. `gauge` shows a single vital against `thresholds` bands with a text status. `time-series-chart` plots a trend: `series` of `{t, v}` points, `thresholds` with a band (`value` to `to`) for the reference range, brush zoom, keyboard stepping and a built-in data-table fallback, in a named `timeZone`. `stat` for the latest reading and `date-range-picker` for the period.
needs.gap: Reference ranges, flags and units must come from your system of record. `time-series-chart` is not a waveform viewer (ECG) and does not annotate events; always keep the values in a table beside any chart.

needs.notes: `alert` is persistent by default and has info, success, warning and destructive variants, a `banner` mode and an `AlertAction` slot: put an Acknowledge `button` in it and call your backend with the user and time. Use `dialog` when the acknowledgement needs a reason. `approval-card` can also gate an action but its resolved badge always reads Approved or Rejected (it cannot say Acknowledged), so prefer `alert` plus `button`. Do not use `sonner` for clinical alerts.

Patient booking: `stepper` (steps accept a `description`, e.g. the chosen clinician and time) for reason, clinician, time and confirm. `date-time-picker` picks the slot in the clinic's named `timeZone` and can show the same moment in the patient's zone; or a `radio-group` you style as slots. For the confirmation, `order-confirmation` works if you relabel it (`labels.steps`, `title`, `tickets`, `ticketsHeading`, `admitOne`) and put the visit details in the `fields` of one ticket whose `code` is an opaque booking reference. Clinic staff schedules use the `scheduler` block: `resources` are clinicians or rooms, `events` are appointments, with conflict marking and drag or keyboard moves.
needs.gap: `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped: it always prints the email sentence, a Total in money format (a free visit shows 0.00), an order summary of priced lines and a QR ticket. For free visits compose a `ticket-pass`, a `stat` row and `button`s instead. Availability, double-booking rules and reminders come from your scheduling system; `scheduler` only marks overlaps.

needs.notes: Active medications in a `table` (dose, route, frequency columns and a status `badge`); `repeater-field` edits multi-line prescriptions, each row built with `field`, `input` and `select` in `renderRow`. Confirm signing in a `dialog` that names the patient and drug. `approval-card` can wrap an order summary with `approveLabel` set to the action, but its resolved badge always says Approved, so use it only where that wording is acceptable.
needs.gap: No drug-interaction or dose-check UI, and no medication-specific component; interaction warnings come from your clinical decision support service and are shown with a persistent `alert`.

needs.notes: `video-player` plays recorded video (patient education, a pre-visit explainer) with captions, chapters and speed. For the live visit, controls (mute, camera, leave) are icon `button`s with `tooltip`s, a waiting-room state is a `badge`, connection quality is a `status-indicator` with a label override, and a connection warning is an `alert`. `avatar` fills a tile when the camera is off.
needs.gap: `video-player` plays a file or stream URL; it is not a call surface. No live video tile grid or device check: embed a video SDK and lay out the tiles yourself. For an in-visit text chat compose `message`, `message-bubble` and `prompt-input` (leave `models` empty).

needs.notes: `stepper` (with step `description`) splits a long form into short steps; `field` and `FieldGroup` give labels, hints and inline errors; `repeater-field` for medications and allergies; `address-form` for the home address; `photo-capture` (camera or file) for insurance card and ID photos, `dropzone` for documents. Consent is signed with `signature-pad` (drawn or typed name) beside the consent text. `question-card` suits a short screening questionnaire: one question at a time, single choice auto-advances, `onSubmitted` returns the answers by index.
needs.gap: Store the signature with a timestamp and the consent text version in your backend; the pad only returns an image. No rich text editor needed here. For date of birth use three `input`/`select` fields: `date-picker` only has previous and next month buttons, so going back decades is slow. `question-card` always shows a Skip action and a free-text 'Something else' option and has no scoring or branching.

needs.notes: `timeline` is a strong fit for encounters and events: statuses (success, warning, destructive, current, upcoming) never rely on color alone, mono timestamps, an `items` array, expandable detail for notes or attachments, and collapsible long lists. `progress` with `label` and `valueLabel` for goals (`3 of 5 sessions`). `checklist` for care-plan tasks the patient or nurse ticks off, with notes per item and a sign-off step. `rich-text-editor` for clinical notes (formatting toolbar, link validation, character limit) with its read-only renderer for display.
needs.gap: Clinical documentation standards, templates and coding are your system's job; the editor only captures formatted text (HTML or JSON) and does not autosave or track versions.

needs.need: Secure messaging with the care team
needs.notes: `message` rows (`from` is `user` or `assistant`, mapped to patient and clinician) with `avatar`, a header for name and time, and a footer for 'Read 14:02' text; `message-bubble` variants; `message-scroller` for the transcript; `prompt-input` as the composer (omit `models` to hide the model picker). `chat-app` is the shell with a folding sidebar, and the thread list is built with `animated-sidebar`. Keep an `alert` visible saying messages are not for emergencies.
needs.gap: No attachment preview, read-receipt logic, thread list data model or clinician routing (only the slots to render them); only two sides (`user`/`assistant`). Keep the thread data on your own secure backend.

needs.need: Sign in with MFA and a proxy or caregiver
needs.notes: `auth-screen` handles email and password (and optional provider buttons); after its `onSubmit` resolves, show `mfa-step` (`methods`, async `onVerify`, `onResend` with a countdown, error and locked states). Caregiver access can use the `team` section of `settings-page` (members with an invite by email and a role); a `permission-matrix` can show what each proxy role may see.
needs.gap: `settings-page` roles are fixed to owner, admin, member and viewer (viewer is the nearest to a read-only proxy), and the section has no consent scope or expiry, so build those with `switch`, `date-picker` and a `data-table`. Verification of the code is your auth provider's job.

integrations.note: opendraft is presentation only; map FHIR resources to the props of `table`, `stat` and `timeline` in a thin adapter and keep PHI out of client logs.
video-player covers recorded video; the SDK renders the live call. Use opendraft buttons, badges and `alert` for controls, waiting-room state and connection warnings around it.

time-series-chart ships axes, threshold bands, keyboard stepping and a data-table fallback; use a charting library only for clinical waveforms or dense annotations, styled with the semantic tokens and with a text legend.

The scheduler block covers clinician schedules (resource day and week views); embed one of these only for recurrence or very large calendars, and keep date-time-picker and radio-group for the patient-facing booking path.
signature-pad captures a drawn or typed signature as an image; store it with a timestamp and the consent text version. Use these services for legally binding e-signature and identity verification.

domains.title: Fintech and banking
domains.summary: Banking, payments, trading, personal finance and lending products. Money moves, so precision, clear fees and honest balances matter more than delight; many actions cannot be undone.
principles: Format money with the locale and ISO 4217 currency (`Intl.NumberFormat`), show the currency on every amount that might be ambiguous, align figures right in `tabular-nums` and keep minor units. Never compute with floating point; use integer minor units or a decimal library.

Treat transfers, payouts and trades as irreversible: show a review step with payee, amount, fee, rate and arrival time, then confirm. Require step-up authentication (a one-time code or biometric) before a high-risk action.
Show every fee, rate and the final total before the user commits, not after. If the amount can change (FX, market orders), say so and show when the quote expires.
Be honest about balance: label Available versus Pending versus Current, show `as of` time, and mark data that is delayed. Never show an optimistic balance as if it had settled.

Never use red and green alone for gain and loss; add a sign and an arrow or word (`+2.4%`, `Down`). `stat`'s `delta` does this (arrow plus a screen-reader word) and `goodWhen` says which direction is good news, so a falling expense reads as good. Do not use red for a number that is merely negative in an accounting sense when it is not an error.

Keep an audit trail the user can see (activity, statements, who approved what) and mask account and card numbers by default, showing only the last four digits with an explicit reveal and `copy-button`.

opendraft is presentation only: it does not move money, price orders or check balances, and nothing here is a compliance or regulatory guarantee. Show regulatory disclosures and risk warnings your jurisdiction requires as plain text next to the action, and take quotes, balances and fees only from your backend.

needs.notes: `stat` tiles for each account: `value` and `hint` accept ReactNode, so pass a pre-formatted string and an `as of` hint; `delta` gives a signed change with an arrow. `animated-number` takes a plain number and an `Intl.NumberFormat` `format` (for example currency), so use it only for a hero balance and convert from minor units for display only; never inside tables. `time-series-chart` shows balance history with a `unit` formatter and a data-table fallback; `data-table` lists accounts or recent activity.

`data-table` block: `searchable`, `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for account, category, status), sortable columns, `views` (All, Pending, Posted), paging and a card layout on phones. Right-align the amount in a `cell` renderer (`mono`, `align="right"`) and render status as `badge` (Pending, Posted, Failed). `selectable` with `bulkActions` (Export, Categorize) receives the selected rows; `copy-button` for a reference id. For years of history use the virtualized `table` with `onEndReached`.
needs.gap: No saved searches. Date narrowing is by calendar day (`date-range-picker`); use `date-time-picker` for exact bounds. CSV export and statement PDFs are yours to build.

needs.need: Send money / transfer with review and step-up auth
needs.notes: `stepper` flow (payee, amount, review, verify, done; `description` can carry the chosen payee). Review step is a `description-list` or `stat`/`StatGroup` of payee, amount, fee, rate and arrival, then a confirm `button` (optionally in a `dialog`). `mfa-step` for step-up (`methods`, async `onVerify`, `onResend` with a countdown, error and `locked` states). Receipt: `alert` success, `description-list` with a `copyable` reference and a `timeline` of the transfer status (initiated, processing, arrives).
needs.gap: No review or receipt component. `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped (QR tickets, qty by price lines, email sentence) and `approval-card` ends with an Approved badge, so neither suits a transfer. `mfa-step` only collects the code; verification, limits and lockout policy are your backend's.

needs.notes: The `checkout` block is built for ticket and booking purchases: details step is name, email, phone, an 'I'm booking for someone else' attendee and a delivery choice (digital pass by email or collect at front desk), payment is card or pay later, and the confirmation prints a ticket pass per item. Most of this copy is fixed. Build a payment form from `field`, `input` and `radio-group` (saved methods as radio cards), `address-form` for the billing address (per-country postal rules), a `stepper`, and mount your provider's hosted fields for the card.
needs.gap: `checkout` does not fit bank or card products and its card form cannot be lifted out of the block. There is no card-number component: card entry belongs in your provider's hosted fields. Compose the rest from primitives.

needs.notes: Holdings in `data-table` with a signed change cell (sign, arrow or word, not color alone). `time-series-chart` plots portfolio value or a price line: several `series`, a named `timeZone`, brush zoom, keyboard stepping, thresholds (for example a target) and a data-table fallback. `analytics-dashboard` can be relabelled for portfolio value: KPI metrics take `Intl` `format` (currency), the `channels` share bar can show asset allocation, and `valueColumn`/`formatVisitors`/`formatConversion` repurpose table columns (quantity, weight, value).
needs.gap: No candlestick or OHLC chart, no crosshair across panes, no order book and no live ticker; use a charting library for those and keep numbers in tabular figures. `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7/30/90 days.

needs.notes: `tabs` for Buy and Sell (label them in words); `quantity-stepper` for whole units (`min`, `max`, `step`) or `input` for fractional ones; `slider` with `marks` and `formatValue` for a percent of balance; an order preview in a `dialog` with `stat`s for estimated cost, fees and quote time, and a confirm button. An `alert` for market-closed or price-moved warnings.
needs.gap: No market-depth or order-ticket component; the estimated price must come from your pricing service and show when it was quoted.

needs.notes: `progress` with `tone="auto"` measures consumption by default (a fuller bar turns warning, then destructive), which suits category budgets; set `label` and `valueLabel` (`$320 of $400`). `gauge` shows overall budget used with `thresholds` and a text status. `stat` for totals with `delta` and `goodWhen="down"` for spend. `time-series-chart` for monthly spend against a budget `threshold`. `analytics-dashboard` (relabelled) adds a stacked share bar for category breakdown.
needs.gap: No donut chart and no cash-flow (Sankey) chart; the category breakdown is a single stacked horizontal bar with five tones. `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed at 7, 30 and 90 day tabs (relabel them).

needs.notes: `slider` for amount and term (`formatValue`, `marks`), a live repayment summary in `stat`s, `repeater-field` for income sources or existing debts, `address-form` for the residential address, `dropzone` or `photo-capture` for income documents, and an `alert` plus `timeline` for 'application received' and next steps.
needs.gap: No amortization schedule with built-in calculations; compute it server-side and render it with `table`. `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped, so it is not used for the submitted state.

needs.notes: `stepper` (with `description`) for the checks; `address-form` for the residential address; `photo-capture` takes ID and selfie photos from the phone camera (camera or file, `max`, `facing`); `dropzone` for proof-of-address documents; `mfa-step` for phone or email codes. Show each check with a `status-indicator` using `label` and `tone` overrides (Pending, Verified, Needs attention) or a `badge`.
needs.gap: `photo-capture` only takes still images: there is no live camera preview, document frame overlay or liveness check. Use your identity provider's SDK for those.

needs.notes: Card freeze and alert preferences as `switch` rows, limits with `field` or `slider`, login and device history in `data-table` or `timeline` (mono timestamps, status markers), and a type-to-confirm `dialog` for closing an account. `mfa-step` re-verifies before changing limits. `secret-input` for API tokens on business accounts and `permission-matrix` for what each delegate may do. `settings-page` can supply the grouped switch rows (its `notifications` groups) and a type-to-confirm danger zone (`dangerLabels`, `sections`).
needs.gap: `settings-page` sections are fixed to profile, notifications, team and billing and the danger-zone confirmation requires typing the `workspaceName`; there is no security, devices or limits section, so compose those from the primitives.

integrations.note: Mount the provider's hosted fields inside your own payment form (built from `field` and `radio-group`) so card data never touches your app; send your backend a token only.

integrations.for: Bank account linking and open banking data
integrations.note: These open their own modal; surround it with an opendraft `dialog` that explains what is shared and wait for the result before updating balances.
Pass already formatted strings to `stat` and to `table` cell renderers; keep amounts in integer minor units in your data layer.

time-series-chart ships a line chart with axes, thresholds, zoom and a table fallback. For candlesticks, crosshair or live price charts, theme a library with design tokens and add a text value readout so gain and loss do not rely on color.
Use their SDK for document and liveness capture; photo-capture only takes still photos. Show the outcome with `status-indicator` and `alert`.

domains.title: E-commerce and marketplaces
domains.summary: Storefronts, marketplaces and seller dashboards. Shoppers need honest prices and stock and a fast path to pay; sellers need to manage orders and inventory in bulk.
principles: Be honest about price and availability: show the total with tax, shipping and fees before checkout, strike through a compare-at price only when it is real, and show stock states in words (In stock, Only 3 left, Sold out) from live data. `progress` with `tone="auto"` and `invert` can show remaining stock, but pair it with the words.
Persist the cart across sessions and devices, never silently change a quantity or price, and if something changed since the user added it, say what changed (an `alert`) and let them decide.

Show trust signals where the decision happens: delivery date, return window, secure payment note, ratings with the review count and who can leave a review. Do not invent urgency such as fake countdowns or invented stock numbers.
Offer guest checkout and fast payment options; ask for the fewest fields, validate inline and keep the order summary visible while the user fills the form.
State returns, refunds and shipping costs in plain words before purchase, and give the order status and the next step on every order screen.
Make sold-out and error states useful: offer a back-in-stock notification or similar items, keep filters on a no-results page and keep the user's progress when a payment fails.

Check which opendraft blocks fit before using them: `catalog`, `detail-page`, `checkout` and `order-confirmation` are built for dated, seat-limited, ticketed things (classes, tours, events). For physical goods use `product-card` (with `ProductGrid`), `image-gallery`, `rating` and `address-form` and compose the rest from primitives; the playbook below says which.

needs.notes: `ProductGrid` (from the `product-card` file) lays out `product-card` tiles: `title`, `image` (or `renderImage` for your framework's image), `price` with `compareAtPrice`, `currency`/`locale`, text `badges`, a `rating` slot (pass a `rating` display), `outOfStock` and `onAdd`/`href`. Above it, `filter-bar` gives search, single and multi-select facets (size, color, brand) as removable chips with clear-all, and `select` handles sort. `skeleton` while loading; `empty-state` (with `live`) for no results and a Clear filters action that keeps the other filters.
needs.gap: `filter-bar` renders the controls from a config; you compute the facets and counts and filter or query your own data (`search-list` takes plain strings only). No price-range slider facet, no infinite scroll or pagination component. `catalog` is not for retail products: every item requires `host`, an ISO `date`, `capacity` and `remaining`.

needs.need: Sell bookable things: classes, tours, workshops, tickets
needs.notes: This is what the blocks are built for. `catalog` (search, category chips, sort, price buckets, availability switch, grid or compact list, ISO `currency`) lists items shaped title, host, location, category, date, price, capacity, remaining. `detail-page` shows media, key facts, About, Schedule and FAQ tabs, tiers with quantity, running total, checkout and waitlist (`onWaitlist`, relabel to Notify me via `labels`). `checkout` takes `items`, `fees`, `currency`, `discountCodes` and an async `onPay` that gets masked card data (last four only). `order-confirmation` and `ticket-pass` give the receipt and QR passes. Map `DetailCheckout` ({tierId, quantity}) to `CheckoutItem`s yourself.

needs.need: Product detail with variants and purchase panel
needs.notes: Compose: `image-gallery` for the main image with thumbnails, keyboard and swipe navigation and a click-to-zoom lightbox (`images` need real `alt` text); `rating` (display) with the review count; `tabs` or `accordion` for description, specs, shipping and returns, with specs in `description-list`; `radio-group` styled as size chips or swatches for variants (disable out-of-stock options); `quantity-stepper` with `max` set to stock; a `badge` for In stock or Sold out; `progress` with `tone="auto"` and `invert` for a low-stock bar; a primary `button` plus a Notify me action when sold out.
needs.gap: `detail-page` is an event-ticket page, not a product page: it requires `date` and a `host` and its options are seat-limited 'tiers'. There is no variant picker or swatch component, no size guide and no 360 or video media in `image-gallery` (use `video-player` for a product video).

needs.notes: `rating` shows stars with half steps, a text value and a count (`Rating` with `value`, `count`) and a distribution breakdown (rows per star count); as an input (`RatingInput`) it takes `onValueChange`, `allowHalf`, `required` and keyboard arrows for the review form. Reviews are your own list with `avatar`, a 'Verified purchase' `badge` only when you can verify it, `accordion` for long text and `textarea` for the form body.
needs.gap: No review list, sorting or helpful-vote component; show only reviews you can verify and moderate them in your backend.

needs.notes: A cart in a `drawer` (side sheet, closes on Esc or backdrop; you supply the header, since it has no title slot) with `quantity-stepper` lines (`max` = stock), a subtotal and a checkout `button`; `empty-state` when empty; `alert` when a price or availability changed; `sonner` for 'added to cart' feedback.
needs.gap: No cart component: build the line list yourself and persist the cart on your backend. `checkout` has a quantity-stepper order summary but only inside its ticket flow.

needs.need: Checkout (guest or account) and payment for physical goods
needs.notes: Build with `stepper` (shipping, delivery, payment, review; steps take a `description`), `address-form` for shipping and billing addresses (per-country postal and region rules, validation and correct autocomplete tokens), `radio-group` for shipping methods (price and arrival date in each option), `checkbox` for billing same as shipping, an order summary list with totals, a discount code `input`, and your payment provider's hosted fields and wallet buttons.
needs.gap: The `checkout` block cannot do this: its details step is Full name, Email, Phone and an 'I'm booking for someone else' attendee, then a delivery choice of 'Digital pass by email' or 'Collect at the front desk' (hard-coded), payment is card or 'Pay later (within 3 days)', and the confirmation prints a QR ticket pass per item. There is no shipping-method picker, order-summary component or wallet-button slot, and `address-form` does not look up addresses. Tax and shipping rates come from your backend.

needs.notes: `timeline` is a ready tracking view: statuses success, current and upcoming for Placed, Packed, Shipped and Delivered, `timestamp` and `time`, `meta` for the carrier or location, expandable detail for scan events, and a loading state. `stepper` (steps accept `description` for an estimated date) for the coarse stages; `copy-button` for the tracking number; `alert` for a delay. Order totals in `stat`s and your own line list.
needs.gap: `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped: it always prints 'A confirmation was sent to' with the email, a Tickets stat, a 'Your tickets' section with a QR pass per ticket (an empty list leaves a bare heading), a priced line list, and a stepper that is always fully completed (Details, Payment, Confirmation), with no shipping status. Use it only for tickets and bookings.

needs.notes: A `stepper` flow: choose items (`checkbox`), reason (`select`), notes (`textarea`), photos with `dropzone` (`accept`, `maxFiles`, `capture`), then refund or exchange (`radio-group`) and a review step; show the return deadline in an `alert`.
needs.gap: No printable return-label view; render it from your carrier's PDF.

needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for revenue, orders and conversion: metrics have `Intl` `format` and a delta vs the previous period, there is a single-series line chart with metric tabs, a sortable table (name, visitors, conversion 0-1, and a custom `valueColumn` for revenue) and a stacked share bar in `channels`. For your own series (revenue against last period, orders per hour) use `time-series-chart`: several series, a named `timeZone`, brush zoom and a data-table fallback.
needs.gap: The `analytics-dashboard` range tabs are fixed to 7d, 30d and 90d and are not driven by `date-range-picker`; its table columns are page-analytics shaped; only one stacked bar for breakdowns, no donut.

needs.notes: `data-table` block: `views` for New, To ship and Returns, `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for channel, carrier, date), a status `badge` in a `cell`, `selectable` with `bulkActions` (Print labels, Mark shipped receive the selected rows), paging and a card layout on phones. A `progress` bar in a stock cell with `tone="auto"` and `invert`. For very long order lists use the virtualized `table` with `filter-bar` and `bulk-action-bar`.

needs.need: Create and edit a product listing
needs.notes: `field` and `FieldGroup`, `rich-text-editor` for the description (formatting toolbar, validated links, `maxLength`; store its HTML or JSON and render with its read-only renderer), `repeater-field` for variants and prices (rows built in `renderRow`), `dropzone` or `photo-capture` for photos (`multiple`, `accept`, `maxFiles`), `image-gallery` for a storefront preview, `switch` for published, `stepper` to split a long form.
needs.gap: No image reordering or cropping. Sanitize rich text on the server before it reaches a storefront.

needs.notes: A `data-table` of codes (sortable, status `badge`, `filters` for active and expired), a `dialog` with a `field` form to create one, `date-range-picker` for the validity window and `switch` to enable it.

integrations.note: Map products, carts and orders to the props of `product-card`, `data-table` and `timeline` in an adapter; map to `catalog`, `detail-page` and `checkout` only for dated, seat-limited items. Keep the cart on the server so it persists across devices.
Mount the provider's hosted card fields and wallet buttons inside your own payment step; send your backend a token only. Tax should come from the provider so the total shown is the total charged.

Drive filter-bar facets and product-card grids from the search results; filter-bar renders the chips but you supply facet options and counts. For event-style items, results can feed `catalog` through its `items` prop.
Show their rates as `radio-group` options in your checkout and their tracking events in a `timeline`.
rating draws stars with a text value and count, and a distribution breakdown. These services supply the reviews; display only reviews you can verify.

domains.title: Education and learning
domains.summary: Learning platforms, courses, classrooms and student information systems. Learners need to know where they are and what is next; instructors need to see a whole class at a glance and act in bulk.
principles: Make progress visible everywhere: where the learner is in the course, what is done, what is next and how long it takes. Use `progress` (`label` and `valueLabel`, e.g. `3 of 8 lessons`) and always offer a clear Continue action. Keep the default brand tone, or `success` at 100%: `tone="auto"` treats a full bar as bad.

Accessibility first: sufficient contrast, full keyboard use, captions and transcripts for media, readable text sizes, no time limits that cannot be extended, and no meaning by color alone. Learners often use shared, older or assistive devices.

Give low-pressure feedback: say what was right and what to try next, avoid red-X shaming, let learners retry, and show a grade only when the instructor chooses to release it. Celebrate completion without confetti that cannot be turned off.

Separate instructor and learner views: the same course shows authoring, grading and class analytics to instructors, and only the learner's own work and progress to students. Never expose other students' names or grades.
Be offline-tolerant: save drafts and answers locally as the learner types, show a visible Saved or Not saved state, and queue submissions with a clear status when the connection drops.

Protect minors' data: avoid public profiles by default, show only what a guardian or teacher needs, and put sensitive records behind explicit access. Where your rules require it, keep consent and access records; opendraft makes no compliance guarantee.

needs.notes: Works for cohort or scheduled courses. `catalog`: `host` is the instructor (set `labels.hostLabel` to 'Taught by'), `date` the start date, `capacity` and `remaining` the seats, `category` the subject, `priceRanges` and `currency` for fees (price 0 shows the free label). `detail-page`: tiers are enrolment options (full price, concession), the Schedule tab is the week-by-week outline, key facts for length and level, FAQ, `onWaitlist` for full cohorts; relabel with `labels`. `checkout` for paid enrolment.
needs.gap: Item shape is event-shaped: `host`, `date`, `capacity` and `remaining` are required and the date block and seats are always shown, so self-paced courses with no start date or seat limit don't fit (use `card`, `input`, `select` and `badge`). No prerequisite or level filters. `checkout` has fixed copy (booking for someone else, digital pass or desk collection, a QR ticket on confirmation); free enrolment can skip it and call your API from `onCheckout`.

needs.notes: One `card` per course with `progress` (`label` is the course, `valueLabel` '3 of 8 lessons') and a Continue `button`; `stat` for streak or time spent; `tabs` for In progress and Completed; `empty-state` for a new learner. Don't set `tone="auto"` on completion bars: it reads a full bar as bad.

`step-nav` is the syllabus: `steps` with status complete, current, available or locked (a `lockedReason` explains why), non-linear jumping with `onSelect`, a `{done} of {total} complete` summary and a vertical layout for a sidebar or horizontal for a short path. Group modules in an `accordion` with a `step-nav` inside, or use an `animated-sidebar` menu (menu buttons with `isActive`, `disabled`, a `badge` slot, sub-menus, a mobile sheet) around it. `progress` for the module. `sidebar-nav` is an AI chat sidebar, not course navigation.

`video-player` for the lesson video: seek, volume, speed, captions (`tracks`), `chapters`, keyboard shortcuts, `startAt` to resume, `onProgress` to report watched time into `progress`, and an error state with retry. `transcript-viewer` and `audio-player` for podcasts and audio lessons. `document-viewer` is the shell for slides and PDFs: page navigation, zoom, search and download with thumbnails; it renders pages through `renderPage` or `src`. Transcript, notes and resources sit in `tabs` beside the player; `accordion` for chapters; `code-block` for programming lessons.
needs.gap: `document-viewer` is a shell, not a PDF engine: you supply the page rendering (for example with PDF.js) or an embeddable `src`. `video-player` plays a file or HLS-capable source; DRM, adaptive streaming setup and watch-time analytics come from your video host.

needs.notes: Compose a quiz: `radio-group` and `checkbox` for answers, `textarea` for short answers, `progress` with `label` '4 of 10', a `dialog` that confirms submit and names unanswered questions, and an `alert` for time remaining. Keep scoring and explanations in your code and show them with `badge` and `alert`. `question-card` suits ungraded warm-up questions or polls.
needs.gap: `question-card` is survey-shaped, not a quiz: questions are `{q, type, options}` strings with no correct answer, single choice auto-advances so answers cannot be reviewed first, there is always a Skip button and a free-text 'Something else' option, and it returns answers by index with no scoring or feedback. No timer with accessibility extensions, no question-bank authoring.

needs.notes: `dropzone` for uploads (`accept`, `maxSize`, `maxFiles`, a `files` list with progress and per-file error; you handle the upload), `rich-text-editor` for a written answer, `photo-capture` to photograph handwritten work, a status `badge` (Not started, Submitted, Late, Graded), `timeline` for submission history, and an `alert` for the deadline.

`table` is the grid: virtualized (fixed `rowHeight`, `height`), sticky header, sortable, resizable and reorderable columns, `selectable` with `onSelectionChange` (ids) and `getRowId`, and `editable` columns with `onCellEdit` for inline score entry (plain text input, so validate the number yourself). `filter-bar` above it for section and status, and `bulk-action-bar` over the selection (Release grades, Send reminder). Open feedback in a `drawer` with `textarea` (or `rich-text-editor`) and a `slider` per rubric criterion (`marks`, `formatValue`). For a small class `data-table` also gives cards on phones.
needs.gap: No rubric component and no sticky first column. The virtualized `table` scrolls sideways on phones. Grade calculation and release rules belong in your backend.

needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard`: KPI cards with delta (completion, average score), one metric line chart with tabs, a sortable table per assignment, and the `channels` stacked bar can show grade bands. `time-series-chart` plots your own series (submissions per day against the deadline, several cohorts) with `thresholds` and a data-table fallback. `gauge` for cohort completion with a text status; `progress` per assignment.
needs.gap: `analytics-dashboard` ranges are fixed to three tabs (7d, 30d, 90d; relabel to week, month, term) and are not driven by `date-range-picker`. No histogram and no per-student drill-down chart.

needs.notes: `scheduler` block for a timetable: `resources` are rooms, classes or teachers, `events` are sessions, with day and week views and an agenda on narrow widths. `gantt` for a term plan with assignment due dates and dependencies. `timeline` lists upcoming deadlines in order (`time`, `timestamp`, status current, upcoming or destructive for overdue, `meta` for the course); `alert` for due soon; `date-time-picker` to set a reminder or a due time in a named `timeZone`.
needs.gap: `scheduler` is a resource day and week view, not a month grid with event dots; no recurrence rules or iCal sync, so expand repeats and export calendars in your backend.

needs.notes: `message` rows (`from` is `user` or `assistant`) with `avatar`; `prompt-input` as the composer (omit `models`); `streaming-response` for tutor answers (status streaming, complete or error, copy, retry, up or down feedback, and a `sources` list); `citations` lets a tutor point to course material; `message-scroller` follows streamed output. For longer forum posts use `rich-text-editor` with its read-only renderer. Label AI answers clearly.
needs.gap: No threaded forum with replies, reactions or moderation, and no instructor review queue; only two message sides. Build those from `message` and `table`.

integrations.note: video-player covers captions, chapters, speed and resume; use these only for adaptive streaming, DRM or analytics. Report progress back to update `progress` and place the transcript beside it.
These sit in your backend; opendraft only renders the resulting course, grade and progress data, so map them into the props of `progress`, `table` and `stepper`.

integrations.for: Rostering and sign-in with school accounts
integrations.note: `auth-screen` takes a `providers` list for the provider buttons but always shows the email and password form; keep roles (student, teacher, guardian) in your own data so views can differ.
Save answers and drafts locally and show a Saved or Queued state with `badge`; flush the queue on reconnect.
scheduler (resource day and week views) and gantt (term plans) ship. Use one of these for month grids and recurrence, and keep the opendraft `timeline` for a simple upcoming-deadlines list.

domains.title: Energy, utilities and EV charging
domains.summary: Grid operations, smart metering, solar and storage, EV charging networks, field service and customer billing for electricity, gas and water providers. Numbers carry units, time carries a zone, and some actions can hurt people or equipment.
principles: Always show the unit and the magnitude together, in `font-mono` with `tabular-nums`: `4.2 kW`, `18.6 MWh`, `230 V`. `stat` takes any node as `value`, so wrap the number and unit in a `font-mono` span. Do not auto-switch between W, kW and MW inside one column; pick one unit per column and say it in the header.

Be honest about time series. Label the interval and aggregation (15-min average, hourly sum, daily peak), mark gaps and estimated reads as such instead of drawing a line through them, and never smooth data without saying so.

Outage and alarm severity uses a fixed scale with a word and an icon, not color alone (for example Critical, Major, Minor, Advisory). Show start time, affected customers or assets, and estimated restoration time with its source.

Switching, isolating or energizing equipment is guarded by interlocks: show the current state, the precondition that blocks the action, and require a confirmation that names the asset and consequence. Show who did it and when, and never allow a one-click remote switch.

Show every timestamp with its zone, and show the asset's own local time beside the operator's. Grids span regions, and daylight saving shifts create 23- and 25-hour days; billing periods and tariffs must follow the meter's zone. `time-series-chart`, `scheduler` and `date-time-picker` take a named IANA `timeZone` (`date-time-picker` handles DST gaps and overlaps); `date-picker` and `date-range-picker` work on plain calendar dates with no zone, so keep the zone in your own data and print it next to the value.
Separate measured, estimated and forecast values visually and in text (solid, dashed, labeled). A billing or settlement figure always shows its status: actual, estimated or disputed.

needs.notes: `stat` tiles for load, generation and frequency (unit inside `value`, `delta` with `goodWhen` for the change chip). `gauge` shows loading against a limit with `thresholds` bands and a text status. `status-indicator` gives a shape plus a word; its five built-in statuses are operational, degraded, down, maintenance and unknown, and `label`, `tone` and `shape` override them for words like Energized or Islanded. `progress` with `tone="auto"` shows headroom against a limit. `map-view` shows substations and feeders as labelled status markers with a synced list. `alert` for active network notices, `badge` for a text severity.
needs.gap: `stat` has no threshold or limit marking (use `gauge` or `progress` beside it), and there is no single-line diagram or network topology view.

needs.need: Live and historical load, generation and consumption charts
needs.notes: `time-series-chart` is the interval chart: several `series` of `{t, v}` points where a null `v` leaves a visible gap (missing reads are not drawn through), a per-series `dash` for forecast or estimated values, `thresholds` for a capacity limit or a tariff band (a line, or a shaded band with `to`), a `unit` and `formatValue`, a named `timeZone` (so 23- and 25-hour days render correctly), brush zoom with `onZoomChange`, keyboard stepping and a built-in data-table fallback. Drive the range with `date-range-picker` for days or `date-time-picker` for exact bounds. `analytics-dashboard` still suits a KPI-plus-table overview.
needs.gap: One value axis (shared `unit`): no two-axis view and no stacked area for generation mix. Aggregation (15-min average, hourly sum) happens in your backend; the chart does not resample. For tens of thousands of points per series use uPlot or ECharts.

needs.notes: `data-table` block with a meter ID in `mono` plus `copy-button`, read quality as a text `badge` (Actual, Estimated, Missing), `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for feeder, quality, tariff), `views` and `selectable` with `bulkActions` for bulk reads or commands, and a card layout on phones. For hundreds of thousands of meters use the virtualized `table` (pixel `rowHeight`, plus `height` or `maxHeight`) with `filter-bar` and `bulk-action-bar`.

`map-view` shows outages as labelled markers (`status` plus text) with `areas` for affected polygons and `routes` for feeders, `selectedId` synced to a `data-table` of outages with a severity `badge`. Each outage's updates go in `timeline` (`timestamp`, `status`, and `meta` for the author); restoration stages (reported, crew dispatched, repair, restored) in a vertical `stepper` where each step's `description` can carry the time and the estimated restoration source.
needs.gap: `map-view` draws the shapes you pass; it does not compute affected areas, customer counts or crew routes, and it has no heat map layer. `stepper` only makes completed steps clickable.

needs.need: EV charging network and charge point status
needs.notes: Charge points in `data-table` with a `status-indicator` per connector (use `label`, `tone` and `shape` for Available, Charging, Faulted, Offline since the built-in kinds are service-status words) and `filters` for status and connector type. `map-view` shows the stations as labelled markers with a synced list. `gauge` for session state of charge or site load against a limit; `stat` for uptime and energy delivered.
needs.gap: `map-view` has no marker clustering for very large networks or live availability feed; stream status from your backend (OCPP gateway) and update the markers.

needs.need: Start and monitor a charging session (driver)
needs.notes: Enter the charger code with `otp-input` (set `length` and `pattern="alphanumeric"`), show `progress` (brand tone) for charge level, `stat` for kWh, cost and time remaining, and a clear stop `button`. Use `alert` for a faulted connector.
needs.gap: No QR scanner (`qr-code` only renders codes, it cannot read them) and no payment-method selector built for tap-to-pay. `checkout` is an event-ticket flow and does not fit a session payment.
