needs.notes: Production, consumption, export and battery level in `stat` and `gauge` (a low battery warns with a text status; or `progress` with `invert` and `valueLabel` such as `64%`). `time-series-chart` draws the day curve with production, consumption and a dashed forecast series in the site's `timeZone`. `slider` (with `label`, `formatValue`, `marks` and `onValueCommit` so you save on release) and `switch` for reserve level and backup mode.
needs.gap: No energy-flow diagram (solar to home to battery to grid). The chart has one value axis, so plot kW and state of charge in separate charts.

needs.need: Field service work orders and technician dispatch
needs.notes: Work orders in `data-table`; dispatch in the `scheduler` block (`resources` are technicians or crews, `events` are jobs, conflict marking, drag or keyboard reassignment) beside a `map-view` of job sites. Job detail is the `record-page` block (header facts, status, activity `timeline`, related items); `detail-page` is an event-ticket purchase page and does not fit. The safety and completion list is `checklist` (tickable items, notes per item, progress, sign-off); `todo-list` is a read-only plan display. Capture the customer's signature with `signature-pad` and evidence photos with `photo-capture`; supervisor approval through `approval-card`.
needs.gap: `scheduler` marks time overlaps only; skills matching, travel time and routing come from your dispatch system. Offline sync of work orders is your app's job.

needs.notes: Bill summary in `stat`, line items in `data-table`, usage over the period in `time-series-chart` (with tariff bands as threshold bands), budget used in `progress` (consumption tone), a statement period chosen with `date-range-picker`, bill status as a `badge` (Paid, Open, Disputed). `document-viewer` can show the bill PDF page by page (you supply the page rendering or `src`), with a download link. Build the payment form from `field`, `input`, `address-form` and `radio-group`, with the provider's hosted card fields.
needs.gap: `checkout` and `order-confirmation` are event-ticket shaped (attendee, front-desk delivery, ticket passes) and `settings-page` billing is a SaaS plan panel with a fixed Change plan button, so none fit a utility bill. Tariff calculation is your billing system's job.

needs.need: Demand response, switching and control actions
needs.notes: Build the typed-name confirmation yourself in a `dialog` with an `input` that must match the asset name before the confirm `button` enables. `approval-card` shows the parameters in its `children` with Approve, Request changes and Reject (`approveLabel` is relabelable) for one decision; `sonner` for the result; `timeline` for who did what and when; `table` for the pending requests.
needs.gap: `approval-card` is a single decision with no approver identity, time or reason field, so two-person sign-off (two cards or two statuses) and the recorded actor come from your code. Interlock rules and permissions come from your control system.

integrations.for: Time-series charts for load, generation and meter data
integrations.note: time-series-chart handles gaps, forecast dashes, threshold bands and DST-correct zones for typical interval views; theme uPlot or ECharts with the color tokens only when you plot tens of thousands of interval reads.

integrations.for: Maps of outages, substations, feeders and charge points
integrations.note: map-view is built on MapLibre GL JS with token-styled labelled markers, routes and areas, and a synced list. Use the library directly for heat maps or very large layers, and encode severity with shape and label as well as color.
Stream into `table` and `stat` and keep the last-update time visible; show a stale state when the feed drops rather than the last value as if it were current.

integrations.for: Time zones, daylight saving and interval math
integrations.note: Do billing and interval aggregation in the meter's zone, and format with the zone abbreviation next to `font-mono` timestamps.

integrations.for: Payments for charging sessions and bills
integrations.note: Build the payment form with `field` and `input` (opendraft's `checkout` is an event-ticket flow) and let the provider's hosted fields handle card data.

integrations.for: Barcode and QR scanning for meters, chargers and assets
integrations.note: opendraft's `qr-code` only draws codes; add a scanner component and show a manual-entry `field` as the fallback.

domains.title: Government and civic services
domains.summary: Public-sector portals for permits, licences, benefits, tax, records requests, case management and civic engagement. Used by everyone, including people in stress, on old phones and with assistive technology, so clarity and access come before polish.
principles: Write in plain language: short sentences, common words, one idea per paragraph, the action in the button label (`Apply for a parking permit`, not `Submit`). Explain any term of art the first time it appears.

Design to a high accessibility bar (aim for WCAG 2.2 AA or better; in many places public bodies are legally required to): visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, full keyboard use, errors announced and linked to their fields (`field` wires the ids and ARIA), no information by color alone, and a tested screen reader path for every form. opendraft's components do not make a page compliant by themselves, so test the finished screen.

Long forms must be save-and-resume: ask one thing per step, show the steps with a `stepper`, let people leave and return with a reference number, never lose entered data on an error, and offer a final review page before submission. Neither `stepper` nor `field` stores anything, so draft saving is your backend's job.

Be transparent about status: every application shows its reference number in `font-mono` with a `copy-button`, the current stage in words, what happens next, the expected time, and who to contact. Never leave a person guessing.

Support many languages and reading directions from the start: text can grow 30 to 40 percent, names and addresses are not a US shape, dates and numbers follow the locale, and the language switcher is always visible and labeled in its own language.

No dark patterns: no pre-ticked consent, no countdown pressure on benefits, equal prominence for decline and accept. Ask only for data you need and explain why. Assume a poor connection and an old device: keep pages light, show upload progress, retry safely, and always offer a phone, paper or in-person alternative.

needs.need: Apply for a permit, licence or benefit (multi-step form)
needs.notes: `stepper` for stages (each step takes a `description`, and only completed steps are clickable) or `step-nav` when people may jump between sections and later ones stay locked until earlier ones are done. `field` for label, hint and linked error (`FieldSet` for a legend around radio groups), `address-form` for postal addresses with per-country rules, validation and correct autocomplete tokens, `repeater-field` for household members or prior addresses (`min`, `max`, `renderRow`, `createItem`). `date-picker` takes ISO dates with `min`, `max`, `locale` and `isDateDisabled`. Build the check-your-answers page from `description-list` grouped by step, with a change link per group.
needs.gap: No built-in save-and-resume or draft persistence (store drafts server side) and no address lookup (`address-form` validates what is typed). There is no dedicated check-your-answers component; `description-list` is the building block.

needs.notes: `dropzone` validates `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`, reports `onReject` reasons (file-too-large, file-invalid-type, too-many-files), opens the phone camera with `capture="environment"`, and renders a file list from `files` with per-file `progress`, `error` and `onRemove`. `photo-capture` is the phone-first alternative for photographing a document (camera or file, `max`, optional captions). Show accepted types and size in a `field` hint, and a `badge` for Uploaded or Needs attention. Neither has upload logic: you run the upload and feed `progress` back. Always keep a plain file-input path working.

`stepper` (vertical, with `description` for the expected date) for the stage, `timeline` for dated events (received, in review, more information needed, decided; `timestamp`, `status`, `meta` for who), `description-list` for the application facts, `badge` with words for status, `copy-button` for the reference number, `alert` when action is needed from the applicant. The `record-page` block assembles header, status, summary, details and activity in one go. `detail-page` is an event-ticket purchase page, so do not use it.

`auth-screen` is email and password with sign-in and sign-up tabs, a remember checkbox, a forgot-password callback, optional `providers` buttons (use one per identity provider) and a brand panel. `mfa-step` for the second factor: `methods` (authenticator app, SMS, and a non-SMS route), async `onVerify`, `onResend` with a countdown, and error and `locked` states. `secret-input` for entering a reference or recovery code with reveal.
needs.gap: No digital identity (eID, login.gov style) hand-off flow and no knowledge-based verification; wire your identity provider and show its error states in `alert`. Code verification and lockout come from your backend.

needs.notes: Case queue in `data-table` (`selectable` with `bulkActions` such as Assign; `filter-bar` chips for status, officer and priority; `views` for My cases and Unassigned) or as a `stage-board` (Received, In review, Decision, with drag or keyboard moves and WIP limits). The case file is the `record-page` block: header facts, status, activity `timeline` as the case history, related cases and `tabs` for documents and notes. `document-viewer` shows uploaded documents (you supply page rendering or `src`), `rich-text-editor` for case notes, and `checklist` for eligibility checks with a sign-off. Decisions go through `approval-card` (put a `textarea` for the reason in its `children`; it has Approve, Request changes and Reject but no reason field or decision log of its own). `drawer` for a quick preview.
needs.gap: No SLA timers or automatic assignment; those and the decision log come from your case system. `detail-page` is an event-ticket page and does not fit.

needs.need: Book an appointment or inspection slot
needs.notes: Citizen booking: `date-time-picker` in the office's named `timeZone` (it handles DST and can show the same moment in another zone), or `date-picker` (`min`, `max`, `isDateDisabled` for closed days) plus a `radio-group` of times with booked slots `disabled`. `ticket-pass` makes a confirmation pass with a QR `code`, fields and a status (valid, used, expired, void). Staff manage capacity in the `scheduler` block (`resources` are officers or inspection teams, conflict marking, drag or keyboard moves).
needs.gap: No patient-facing availability grid showing open and booked slots (compose it with `radio-group`), and availability, reschedule and cancel rules come from your booking system. `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped with a fixed three-step stepper.

needs.need: Pay a fee, fine or tax
needs.notes: Show amount, due date and what it is for in `stat` and a short `description-list` or line-item `data-table`. Build the payment form from `field`, `input`, `address-form` (billing address) and `radio-group` with the provider's hosted card fields, and a receipt from `stat`, a `stepper` marked `complete` and a `copy-button` reference.
needs.gap: `checkout` is an event-ticket flow (quantity steppers, attendee, front-desk delivery, pay later, ticket passes) and `order-confirmation` renders ticket passes, so neither fits a fine or tax. Add instalment-plan and concession options yourself.

needs.need: Service notices, closures and emergency banners
needs.notes: `alert` with `banner` for a full-width, dismissible (`dismissible`, `onDismiss`) notice at the top for service disruption or deadlines, with an `AlertAction` button; keep the same severity words across services. `site-header` for the page frame.

needs.need: Find a service, office or document (search and directory)
needs.notes: `search-list` filters a plain list of strings with a live result list and an empty message; `accordion` for FAQs; `empty-state` (`live`) for no results with a next step. For offices and locations, `map-view` shows labelled markers with a synced list (opening hours and accessibility in your own list item via `renderListItem`) beside a `data-table` or list with `filter-bar` for service type. For results that need a description or link, filter your own data into a list.
needs.gap: `search-list` takes strings only. `map-view` has no address search or directions: geocoding and routing come from your provider. `catalog` is event shaped (date, price, capacity, places left) and not a service directory. `command-palette` is a keyboard action menu over in-memory items.

needs.need: Civic data and public dashboards (budgets, performance, open data)
needs.notes: `time-series-chart` plots spending or service volumes: several series, `thresholds` (a budget line or target band), a `unit` formatter, a named `timeZone`, brush zoom, keyboard stepping and a built-in data-table fallback. `analytics-dashboard` pairs a chart with a sortable table: rows are `name`, `visitors`, `conversion` (0 to 1) and `duration`, or a custom `valueColumn` for money; relabel with `labels` and the format props (its tabs are fixed 7d, 30d, 90d, relabel with `labels.ranges`). `gauge` for a single performance measure against a target with a text status, `map-view` for areas, and always keep the numbers in `data-table`.
needs.gap: No bar or choropleth chart; `map-view` markers and areas are not a data-driven shading layer. `analytics-dashboard` has no fiscal-year ranges beyond 90 days, so prefer `time-series-chart` for annual data.

integrations.note: Keep all copy in message files, test with long German and Finnish strings, and set `dir` for right-to-left languages; check each opendraft component in RTL, since some spacing uses left and right classes.

Use auth-screen's `providers` buttons for the identity provider hand-off and its email form as the fallback path, `mfa-step` for second-factor codes, and show a clear error and recovery route when identity checks fail.
Automated tools catch only part of the problems; test each form with a keyboard and a screen reader, and test at 200 percent zoom.
Offer manual entry with `address-form` as the fallback and never block submission when lookup fails; `address-form` validates postal codes per country but does not look addresses up.

Pair with `dropzone` or `photo-capture` for intake (neither has upload logic). `signature-pad` captures a drawn or typed signature and `document-viewer` shows a document you render; use the provider's embedded signing for legally binding signatures.

integrations.for: Notifications by email, SMS and letter
integrations.note: Mirror each notification as a dated entry in `timeline` so a person can see what was sent without needing the message.

domains.title: Manufacturing and industrial operations
domains.summary: Manufacturing execution (MES), shop-floor terminals, quality control, maintenance and industrial IoT dashboards. Used by operators on a feet-and-gloves schedule and by engineers and managers reviewing lines, lots and downtime.
principles: Make state glanceable from across the room. Line, machine and order status uses large type, a word (Running, Idle, Down, Changeover) plus an icon, and high contrast; a wall display needs no reading beyond the status and one number.

Design for gloves and noise: touch targets of at least 56 px on shop-floor terminals, generous spacing, no hover-only or drag-only actions, and confirmations that do not rely on sound alone. opendraft's largest button (`size="xl"`) is 48 px tall and `checkbox`, `radio-group` and `switch` are 16 to 20 px, so enlarge them with classes or wrap each in a full-width 56 px row that carries the click.

Every unit of product has traceability: lot, batch, serial, shift, operator and machine appear on the record, in `font-mono` with a `copy-button` and a scannable code, and corrections add a new entry rather than overwrite an old one.

Rank alarms by priority, not arrival time: Critical (stop and act), Warning (act this shift), Info. Keep alarm text specific (what, where, what to do), require acknowledgement with a name and time, and avoid alarm floods by grouping repeats.

Show shift and time context everywhere: the current shift, shift start, counts since shift start, and timestamps in the plant's local zone. Handovers between shifts need a visible notes and open-issues summary.
Tolerate offline and flaky networks: queue entries locally, show an explicit Saved locally, Syncing and Synced state, never lose a count or a quality reading, and show how stale a displayed value is.

needs.need: Line and machine status wall display (andon)
needs.notes: `stat` tiles for output, target and OEE (`value` takes any node, so wrap the number in a large span or `animated-number`; `delta` with `goodWhen` for against-target), a `status-indicator` per machine (relabel with `label`, `tone`, `shape` for Running, Idle, Down, Changeover), `gauge` for OEE or utilization against `thresholds` with a text status, `progress` (`size="lg"`) for output against target, `alert` for stoppages. `eta-indicator` can show the projected end time of the current order with a confidence word.
needs.gap: No large-format kiosk or full-screen display mode and no auto-rotating screen layout; build it with a scaled container. `stat` renders its value at a fixed `text-3xl`, so check it reads from across the room and enlarge the node you pass as `value`.

needs.need: Production order execution on a terminal
needs.notes: Work instructions as `checklist` (tickable items with notes, progress and a sign-off step) or as `step-nav` (steps complete, current, available or locked, so operators cannot skip ahead; `lockedReason` says why). `todo-list` is a read-only plan display with no tick action, and `detail-page` is an event-ticket page, so neither fits. `quantity-stepper` (`min`, `max`, `step`, hold-to-repeat) for good and scrap counts, `progress` for count against order quantity, `approval-card` or a `dialog` to confirm completion.
needs.gap: Controls are desktop sized (`button` tops out at 48 px, `quantity-stepper` has only `sm` and default), so set larger sizes through classes and verify 56 px targets. No barcode scan input or numeric keypad (use an `input` with `inputMode="numeric"`).

needs.notes: `checklist` for the inspection plan (tickable items, a note per item, progress, sign-off), a `radio-group` (Pass, Fail, N/A) inside a `field` where a step needs a verdict, a measured value in `input`, notes in `textarea`, defect photos with `photo-capture` (camera or file, captions), operator sign-off with `signature-pad` and `approval-card`, and past inspections in `data-table`. `time-series-chart` can draw an SPC run chart: a series of measurements with `thresholds` for the centre line and the upper and lower control limits (or a band with `to` for the tolerance zone). `todo-list` is a read-only plan and `records-table` a fixed contact-list grid, so neither fits.
needs.gap: No dedicated X-bar or R control chart: `time-series-chart` draws the points and limit lines, but the control limits, run rules and Cpk are computed in your backend. No measurement-instrument input.

needs.notes: Alarm list in `data-table` sorted by priority with a text `badge`; `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for area, priority, state), `views` for Active and Acknowledged, `selectable` with `bulkActions` for bulk acknowledge (`selection-actions` is an AI text-rewrite bar, not a bulk bar); `timeline` for the event history; `alert` for the active critical banner. For a high-rate alarm stream use the virtualized `table` with `bulk-action-bar`.
needs.gap: No alarm-shelving or suppression workflow and no audible alarm control; those are logic you build around the table.

needs.notes: OEE, availability, performance and quality in `gauge`, `stat` and `progress`. `time-series-chart` plots OEE or downtime per shift against a target `threshold` in the plant's `timeZone`, with several series, gaps for no-data periods and brush zoom. `analytics-dashboard` can be relabelled for machines: each row is `name` (machine), `visitors` (a count, such as stops), `conversion` (a 0 to 1 rate, such as availability) and `duration` (seconds, such as downtime), with `valueColumn` for one custom number; the share bar can show downtime reasons by percent. `date-range-picker` for custom periods.
needs.gap: No Pareto chart (the share bar has no cumulative line) and no stacked shift-by-shift chart. `analytics-dashboard` range tabs are fixed to the keys 7d, 30d and 90d (relabel them with `labels.ranges` and supply your own data per key).

needs.need: Maintenance work orders and preventive schedules
needs.notes: Work orders in `data-table` (status `badge`, `views` for Open, Due, Done); the planned-maintenance calendar in the `scheduler` block (`resources` are machines or crews, `events` are jobs, conflict marking, drag or keyboard moves) and a shutdown plan in `gantt` (tasks, dependencies, groups, critical flags, today marker). The job page is the `record-page` block with a `checklist` for the procedure (sign-off), history in `timeline` and sign-off in `approval-card`. `date-time-picker` for the planned start in the plant's `timeZone`. `detail-page` is an event-ticket page and `todo-list` is read-only, so they do not fit.
needs.gap: No recurrence rules and no meter-based trigger view (run hours, cycle counts): generate the occurrences and triggers in your CMMS and feed them in.

needs.notes: Search a lot with an `input` that queries your API (`command-palette` filters only an in-memory `items` list, with no query callback, so it suits a small set), show genealogy rows in `data-table`, the lot's facts in `description-list` (`mono`, `copyable` ID values) or the `record-page` block, record history in `timeline`, and a label preview with `qr-code`. `records-table` is a fixed contact-list grid and does not fit.
needs.gap: No tree or graph view for forward and backward genealogy (`flowchart` is a two-card trigger and if-else canvas), and no barcode formats other than QR (Code 128, DataMatrix).

needs.notes: Current readings in `stat` and `data-table` with unit and last-update time; `gauge` (`variant` ring or arc, `thresholds` bands, a text status) for a reading against its limits. `time-series-chart` trends a sensor: several series, `thresholds` for alarm limits, gaps where the feed dropped, brush zoom and a data-table fallback. `slider` (`onValueCommit`) and `switch` can drive setpoints, behind a `dialog` confirmation.
needs.gap: No P&ID or floor-plan view. `time-series-chart` redraws from the series you pass, so stream and window the data yourself. Writes to a PLC need your own interlocks and confirmation.

needs.notes: Stock levels as `gauge` or `progress` with `invert` so low stock warns (the bar measures what remains), in `data-table` with a `filter-bar`; counts with `quantity-stepper`; material requests on a `stage-board` (Requested, Picking, Delivered; drag or keyboard moves); shift handover as `rich-text-editor` or `textarea` posted to a `timeline`, with a `checklist` of open issues to acknowledge.
needs.gap: No barcode scan input. `stage-board` totals use the value you give it; stock accounting stays in your ERP.

integrations.for: Machine and sensor data over industrial protocols
integrations.note: Bridge to the browser through a gateway or WebSocket and show the timestamp from the source, not the browser's receive time, so stale data is obvious.

time-series-chart draws trends, threshold lines and bands with a data-table fallback. Grafana panels can still be embedded beside opendraft `stat` tiles for very high-rate historian data, and uPlot or ECharts suit millions of points.

integrations.for: Barcode and QR scanning on the floor
options: Hardware scanners that act as keyboards
integrations.note: Most scanners type into a focused field; keep one large focused `input` ready and show the scanned value back clearly. `qr-code` only renders codes and `photo-capture` takes still photos, so scanning needs one of these.

integrations.for: ERP, MES and quality system connections
integrations.note: Keep the order, lot and BOM data read through your API and write corrections as new records, which matches the audit trail the UI shows.

integrations.for: Offline-first data and sync on terminals
integrations.note: Surface the Saved locally, Syncing and Synced state with a `badge` and use `sonner` only for failures that need action.
Render the on-screen label with `qr-code` and `font-mono` text, then send the matching ZPL to the printer.

domains.title: HR and people operations
domains.summary: HRIS, recruiting, onboarding, payroll, performance and time-off products used by employees, managers and HR teams. The data is personal and sensitive, so who can see what, and who changed what, is part of the design.
principles: Make views permission-aware: show each person only the fields their role allows, and say so (`Visible to HR only`) rather than leaving a blank. Managers see their reports, employees see themselves, and a view-as preview helps admins check it.

Mask sensitive data by default (salary, national ID, bank details, health and leave reasons, performance ratings) with an explicit reveal that is logged: `secret-input` gives a masked value with reveal, copy and optional auto-hide. Never put such values in URLs, toasts, page titles or exports without a clear warning.

Approval flows show the whole chain: who requested, who must approve now, who is next, what was decided and when. Give every request a status word (Pending, Approved, Declined, Withdrawn) and always allow the requester to withdraw or edit before a decision.

Use inclusive language and flexible data: do not require a binary gender field, allow preferred and legal names, support names that do not fit first and last, and keep pronouns optional. Dates, currencies and working weeks follow the person's country.

Make changes auditable: every edit to pay, title, manager, status or personal data records who, when, old value and new value, visible in a history view. Keep effective dates separate from edit dates so retroactive changes are clear.

Treat people-related decisions with care: show the reason and next step on rejections, avoid ranking people by a single score, label AI-generated summaries or suggestions as such, and keep a human decision-maker on hiring, pay and performance outcomes.

needs.notes: `data-table` block: a searchable table whose name cell renders an `avatar`, role and location, `filters` (`filter-bar` chips for department, location, status), sortable columns and a card layout on phones; a profile in a `drawer` (or its own page with the `record-page` block); jump-to-person with `command-palette` (`label`, `group`, `hint`, `badge` per item, filtered in memory, so it suits a few thousand people at most). `search-list` takes plain strings only, so it cannot show avatars or roles.
needs.gap: No org chart tree or reporting-line visualization: show the manager and direct reports as links in the profile and use a graph or tree library for a full chart. `detail-page` is an event-ticket purchase page, not a person profile.

needs.notes: The `record-page` block is the profile shell (header, status, summary, details, activity `timeline`, related items, extra `tabs`). Show fields in `description-list` (`copyable`, `mono`) with a `badge` such as Visible to HR only; show sensitive values (bank details, national ID) in `secret-input` (masked, reveal, optional auto-hide, copy) and put a `dialog` in front of the reveal when it needs a reason. Edit details with `field` and `input`. `permission-matrix` can document which roles may see which fields.
needs.gap: `secret-input` masks and reveals in the browser only: the logged reveal, the permission check and withholding the value until it is requested are your backend's. `settings-page` has fixed profile fields (name, email, bio, timezone) and a SaaS team and billing layout, and `detail-page` is an event-ticket page, so neither fits.

needs.notes: Request with `date-range-picker` (ISO `{from, to}` dates, `min`, `max`, `presets`), balance in `stat` and `progress` (`valueLabel` such as 12 of 25 days), decision with `approval-card` (Approve, Request changes, Reject; put a `textarea` for a decision note in its `children`), approval chain in `timeline` using `current` and `upcoming` statuses, requests in `data-table`. The team calendar is the `scheduler` block: `resources` are people, `events` are absences (a status word plus `tone`), week view and an agenda on narrow widths.
needs.gap: No half-day support in `date-range-picker`. Do not mark public holidays or weekends with `isDateDisabled`: the range picker refuses any range that spans a disabled day, so people could not book leave across a holiday. Count working days in your own code and show the result next to the range.

needs.notes: `stage-board` block is the hiring pipeline: `stages` (Applied, Screen, Interview, Offer), candidate cards via `renderCard` (`avatar`, role, `badge`), drag or keyboard moves with `onMove`, WIP limits, per-stage totals and a detail panel (`renderDetail`) for the candidate with `tabs`, `timeline` for activity and `approval-card` for an offer decision. A `data-table` with `filter-bar` is the list view of the same candidates. `rating` records a scorecard score (half steps, keyboard arrows) and `rich-text-editor` captures interview notes. `document-viewer` shows a resume you render (or an embeddable `src`). You decide which columns and fields exist, so blind early-stage review is easy.

Steps in `stepper`, fields in `field`, resume upload in `dropzone` (`accept`, `maxSize`, and you run the upload), optional diversity questions as `radio-group` options that include Prefer not to say, an unticked consent `checkbox`, and a confirmation built from `alert` (success), a `stepper` marked `complete` and a `copy-button` reference. `order-confirmation` is ticket-shaped and does not fit.

Tasks per owner (HR, IT, manager, employee) in `checklist` (tickable items, a note per item, progress and a sign-off step) with an owner `badge` and due date, grouped by phase in an `accordion` or `stepper`, documents with `dropzone`, sign-offs with `approval-card`, and completions posted to `timeline`. The first-week plan can be a `scheduler` with the new hire as a resource.
needs.gap: You hold the checked state and ownership rules; `todo-list` is a read-only display of an agent's plan and `task-rows` plays a fixed failed, retry, done animation, so neither works as an interactive checklist.

needs.notes: Run stages in `stepper` (draft, review, approved, paid), differences against the last run in `data-table` with old and new values in custom `cell` renderers (struck-through old, new beside it), final approval via `approval-card`, a `dialog` before submitting, and `dropzone` for imports. Payslips open in `document-viewer` (page navigation, zoom, download; you supply the page rendering or `src`) and bank details show in `secret-input`. `diff-table` is a one-shot demo of an email-directory edit (rows of id, dept, email) and does not take payroll data.
needs.gap: `document-viewer` is a shell, not a PDF engine. Calculation, tax and legal rules come from your payroll provider.

needs.notes: Review cycle in `stepper`, rating with `rating` (stars with text labels), `radio-group` or a `slider` with text `marks` for each level, long-form feedback in `rich-text-editor` (toolbar, link validation, character limit, read-only renderer), goals with `progress`, sections in `tabs`, manager sign-off via `approval-card`. `detail-page` is an event-ticket page and does not fit.
needs.gap: No 9-box or calibration grid (a grid of `stage-board` columns is the nearest start). Keep a human decision-maker on outcomes.

needs.notes: `timeline` for who changed what (`timestamp`, `meta` for the actor, expandable `children` for the old and new value), and a searchable log in `data-table` (sortable, `filters` for actor, field and date, `cell` renderers that show old and new values). `date-range-picker` or `date-time-picker` narrows the period; `description-list` shows one entry. `diff-table` and `filter-table` do not fit: one is a fixed demo shape and the other lists task rows.

needs.need: HR analytics (headcount, attrition, time to hire)
needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for headcount and attrition: metrics each carry a series per range, rows are `name` (department), `visitors` (a count such as headcount), `conversion` (a 0 to 1 rate such as retention) and `duration` (seconds, or use `valueColumn`), and the share bar suits composition. `time-series-chart` plots monthly headcount or time to hire with several series and a target `threshold`. Apply minimum group sizes in your data so small teams cannot be identified.
needs.gap: No funnel or cohort chart. `analytics-dashboard` range tabs are fixed to the keys 7d, 30d and 90d (relabel with `labels.ranges` and supply your own data under each key).

integrations.note: Let the provider own the calculation and show its output in `table` and `stat`; never recompute pay in the browser.
Map their stages onto the `stages` of the `stage-board` and keep candidate notes in your own detail panel rather than copying them.

integrations.for: Single sign-on, provisioning and directory sync
integrations.note: Use SCIM to create and remove accounts at hire and exit, and drive the onboarding checklist from the same events.
signature-pad captures a drawn or typed signature and document-viewer shows a document you render; embed the provider's signing view for legally binding contracts and record the result in `timeline`.

Compute working days and holidays in your own code and show them beside the `date-range-picker`; do not disable holiday dates in the picker, because it rejects ranges that span disabled days. Sync approved leave to the team calendar.
Evaluate on the server and pass the allowed fields to the UI as props, so hidden data is never sent to the browser.

crossDomainGaps.title: Audit-log viewer
crossDomainGaps.why: Security, IT, fintech, HR and government all need who-did-what-when with old and new values, filters, export and tamper-evident cues. Today it is assembled from data-table, filter-bar, description-list and timeline.

crossDomainGaps.title: Notifications center
crossDomainGaps.why: A bell with an unread count, a grouped list, mark-as-read and per-type preferences. Alerts, toasts and banners exist, but no persistent inbox of notifications for operators, patients, learners or buyers.

crossDomainGaps.title: File manager and document library
crossDomainGaps.why: Folders, breadcrumbs, previews, rename, move and share for case files, patient documents, course material and shared drives. dropzone, document-viewer and data-table cover the pieces; there is no tree or folder navigation.

crossDomainGaps.title: Tree view and org chart
crossDomainGaps.why: HR reporting lines, asset hierarchies, forward and backward lot genealogy and permission trees. No expandable tree or hierarchy diagram ships. Recommended base: d3-hierarchy for layout.

crossDomainGaps.title: Node and network graph
crossDomainGaps.why: Attack paths, service dependencies, pipelines and supply chains with pan, zoom and many nodes. flowchart is a small workflow canvas, not a general graph. Recommended base: React Flow.

crossDomainGaps.title: Inbox and thread list
crossDomainGaps.why: Secure messaging, support, case comments and email-style triage need a list of threads with unread state, previews, filters and a reading pane. chat-app covers one conversation, not a mailbox.

integrations.note: MapLibre is open source and needs no vendor key. A themed opendraft map wrapper is on the roadmap.
Read colors from CSS variables so charts follow the theme and dark mode; always offer a table alternative.

integrations.for: Data tables beyond a few thousand rows or with grouping
integrations.note: opendraft's Table is virtualized and covers most needs; reach for these for pivoting, grouping and column pinning.
Use the Field component for labels and errors, and let the schema produce the messages.
Style the editor surface with tokens and keep toolbars to the Button and Toggle patterns.
flowchart covers read-only flows; use these when users edit, pan and zoom.
Until opendraft has a scheduler, embed one and theme it with the CSS variables.
Mount the provider's hosted card fields in the checkout block's card slot so card data never touches your code.
Put the provider behind the auth-screen block; use otp-input for one-time codes.
Update rows in place and announce changes with an aria-live region.
qr-code only generates codes; scanning is a device capability.
Show documents inside a dialog or drawer so the surrounding screen keeps the theme.
